version.changelog: Move to standard skills/<name>/ layout; TypeScript source.

llm.summary: This skill is a repo code-quality reporter that reads source files, creates local report artifacts, and serves a localhost-only HTML report without evidence of exfiltration or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The capabilities match the stated purpose: scan a target repository, compute code-health metrics, generate a report, and provide fix prompts with file/line evidence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The activation language is broad enough to cover generic audit, roast, code-smell, or quality-score requests, so users may see it run even when they did not explicitly name slop-check.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package consists of markdown references, a static HTML template, and dependency-free Node scripts. Metadata static scan is clean, and there are no install hooks or package-install instructions.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: It reads repo source files and writes generated files under .slop-check plus slop-report.html in the target repo. That is coherent for a report generator but can modify the working tree.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It may start a local 127.0.0.1 report server and leave generated report files behind, but shows no privilege escalation, credential handling, external network calls, deletion, or hidden persistence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this if you are comfortable with a skill reading the target repo, creating .slop-check files and slop-report.html, and optionally running a localhost report server. Run it from the repo you intend to grade, and remove the generated files afterward if you do not want them in version control.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger is real, but it is aligned with the skill's repo-grading purpose; the concern is possible surprise activation rather than malicious behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The repo writes are real and should be clearer in the top-level description, but they are the expected output artifacts for the local report workflow.
